mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, which should positively impact the S&P 500 as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate suggests easier monetary policy, which can boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns do not show a positive trend over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production suggests higher economic activity, which can lead to improved market performance.
failure_condition: If industrial production growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased construction activity and economic growth, which can positively impact the stock market.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns do not show a positive trend over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher stock prices.
failure_condition: If payroll employment grows but S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 20 days more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low inflation (CPIAUCSL) and low unemployment (UNRATE) creates a favorable environment for equity markets.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by less than 0.5% and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL and UNRATE move favorably but S&P 500 returns are not positive over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Increased retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, which can boost corporate revenues and stock prices.
failure_condition: If retail sales grow but S&P 500 returns do not show a positive trend over the next 20 days.
